presentation.label: Per-step Note Accumulator
presentation.summary: Each enabled audio step remembers its own pitch increment between visits. Positive values climb, negative values descend, and the pitch wraps to the original note at the chosen range.
presentation.overview: Each enabled audio step remembers its own pitch increment between visits. Positive values climb, negative values descend, and the pitch wraps to the original note at the chosen range.
highlights: OFF or −63 to +63 semitones added on each subsequent visit.
Lock the increment and range for that step.
usage: Load a sample on an audio track, place one note trig and open TRIG.
Set ACC to +1 with G and RNG to 3 with H. Press PLAY: successive visits play the original pitch, +1, +2, +3, then the original again.
For selected steps only, set the track’s ACC to OFF. Hold the desired trig and turn G to a nonzero value; lock RNG with H if needed.
STOP and restart to reset the counters. Set ACC to OFF to bypass accumulation; remove any ACC locks that should also stop accumulating.

limitations: Audio tracks only; every enabled step has an independent counter.
The first accepted play uses the original note. Retrigs retain that visit’s pitch.
Pattern changes and STOP reset temporary counters; ordinary pattern repeats retain them.
Saved settings and locks persist; counters do not. Native pitch limits can cause an early wrap.
RAM-R1 is excluded. Euclidean counters follow source note slots.

load.display: Adds 0.1% average, 1.0% worst-case of an audio block over stock (emulator)
load.conditions: Emulator: OS 1.53 on Core 2.1, 8 audio tracks triggering a full-scale sample and 8 MIDI tracks a note on every step at 120 BPM, 3,000 audio blocks timed with the MCF5441x instruction-timing model at 250 MHz, zero-wait memory. Module workload: ACC +1 on all eight audio tracks. Stock: 59.1% average, 61.8% worst block. All six mods together: 73.2% worst block on 1.53, 73.3% on 1.54. Not a hardware measurement.

hardware.summary: sumedho reports the Core 2.1 all-mods builds fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours in total, including project save and reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14): “ok fully tested on hardware and working”.
limitations: Duration is the reporter’s range (1–2 hours) for the combined session across both OS releases; recorded as 90 minutes.
Individual test outcomes were not itemized; standalone (single-mod) hardware coverage is not claimed.
Tested SysEx: 1.53 23503ca42478c1644dea5fd296893f628eafb6662d2ce5e291bfc591f045ae4e, 1.54 257144e4a584172e470c3dde83d7ccda636eeb195b4e5ff0492b3ebc8bdfaba2; firmware was not read back from the device.

tests.summary: Runs on Core 2.1. Emulator regressions on OS 1.53 and 1.54, an emulator CPU-load comparison with stock, and Modwerk source-build parity with the native build are in TESTING.md. sumedho reports this Core 2.1 build fully tested and working on a Digitakt 1, OS 1.53 and 1.54, for about one to two hours including project save/reload and a power cycle (2026-10-14).
